Customer Intelligence–Enabled Service Resolution

Customers should receive one accurate explanation and a clear next step even when their history spans several banking systems. The proposed capability assembles authoritative service context, uses governed GenAI to interpret what happened, keeps employees accountable for communication and action, and records the outcome as reusable customer intelligence.

Business case

Customer Intelligence–Enabled Service Resolution

Use-case intent

Help a service team resolve repeat or stalled customer requests by reconstructing what happened, identifying the likely blocker, and presenting the appropriate next step.

The use case creates a first practical customer-intelligence asset from fragmented service history. It provides an immediate customer benefit through faster and more consistent resolution.

The corresponding banking-systems, GenAI, agentic, and platform implementation is defined in the Technical Pilot Blueprint.

Problem

A customer contacts the bank several times about the same issue. Calls, chats, cases, complaints, and status changes sit in separate records. The employee must reconstruct the history manually and may miss the actual blocker, repeat an earlier request, or transfer the customer again.

Pilot scope

  • One journey with meaningful repeat-contact or unresolved-case volume.
  • One service team.
  • Recent contact, case, complaint, and status history for that journey.
  • An internal employee view.
  • Employee approval before any customer communication or operational action.

Journey selection and expected benefit

The project selects one journey from a short business-owned candidate list. The entries below are starting points for discussion with Customer Service and the relevant process owner.

Candidate journey Pilot service team Customer problem Primary outcome to test Underlying process owner
Payment issue Payments servicing/contact team customer repeats contact because a failed, pending, or reversed payment and its ownership are unclear fewer repeat contacts and faster confirmed resolution Payments Operations
Card dispute progress Cards or disputes servicing team customer cannot understand progress, evidence needs, or next step fewer status contacts and lower unresolved-case age Disputes Operations
Onboarding/KYC progress Onboarding support team application stalls across document, verification, and review steps fewer repeated information requests and faster progression Customer Onboarding/KYC
Loan application status Lending application support team customer receives fragmented status and is transferred between teams fewer handoffs and clearer committed next step Lending Operations
Complaint resolution and remediation Complaints or specialist resolution team prior contacts have not produced a complete response or durable resolution fewer reopened complaints and stronger resolution quality Complaints owner with affected product operations

Selection should favor high repeat-contact volume, clear process ownership, accessible records, an established resolution process, and a customer outcome that can be measured from existing management information.

Selectable project charters

Three candidate charters apply the common proposal to journey-specific workflows, benefits, risks, and acceptance criteria:

  • Payment Issue Resolution
  • Card Dispute Progress Support
  • Onboarding/KYC Progress Support

Common charter selection and evidence rules apply to all three charters.

Benefit baseline

Before approval, the Benefit Owner and Measurement Owner establish a baseline for the selected journey. The Benefit Owner is accountable for realizing the customer and operational outcome. The Measurement Owner independently defines, calculates, and reports the evidence used to judge it.

Baseline dimension Measures to establish
Customer demand total contacts, repeat-contact rate, contacts per case, reopened cases
Customer resolution first-contact resolution, time to resolution, unresolved-case age, abandoned cases
Customer experience complaints, dissatisfaction, escalations, available satisfaction measures
Operational effort investigation/handling time, handoffs, transfers, manual system checks, rework
Process failure missing information, incorrect routing, unclear ownership, failed step, status inconsistency
Economics cost per contact or case where reliable data exists

The charter selects one primary customer outcome, one operational benefit, and the customer-protection and conduct limits that must remain stable. It records the baseline source, calculation, owner, and target. A useful default is repeat-contact reduction as the primary outcome and investigation effort as the operational benefit.

Business-domain placement

The project sits in the bank's customer-servicing chain:

Customer Service owns the customer interaction, service level, communication, and resolution experience. The selected product-operations function owns the underlying journey and the process steps required to resolve the issue.

Examples of the required pairing are:

Selected journey Customer-facing owner Underlying process owner
payment issue or investigation Head of Customer Service Payments Operations process owner
card servicing or dispute progress Head of Customer Service Cards Operations or Disputes process owner
onboarding/KYC progress Head of Customer Service Customer Onboarding/KYC process owner
loan application status Head of Customer Service Lending Operations process owner
complaint resolution and remediation Head of Customer Service Complaints process owner and affected product-operations owner

The Head of Customer Service is the natural business sponsor. The selected journey process owner is accountable for the correctness of diagnosis, actions, routing, and resolution. Data and delivery specialists build the supporting capability under those business owners.

What is built

For each selected customer case, the service employee receives:

  • the customer's current request;
  • a concise timeline of previous contacts and actions;
  • current case and service status;
  • completed, pending, and failed steps;
  • the likely reason the issue remains unresolved;
  • the approved procedure and proposed next step;
  • links to the underlying records and knowledge sources.

Process integration map

The capability augments the existing servicing workflow at specific points:

Existing process step Existing work Capability introduced by this project Accountable process role
Contact intake identify customer and capture contact reason detect related prior contacts and open cases Service Operations Manager
Triage and routing classify request and select queue propose journey, issue, owner, and urgency from available evidence Journey Process Owner
Investigation search notes and check several systems assemble a single evidence-linked timeline Journey Process Owner
Blocker diagnosis determine why the issue remains open identify completed, pending, failed, or missing process steps Journey Process Owner
Next-step selection interpret procedure and decide what to do present approved procedure and eligible actions Journey Process Owner
Resolution or referral execute, transfer, or escalate carry complete context into the chosen action or referral Service Operations Manager
Customer communication explain current state and expectations provide a source-supported explanation and committed next step Head of Customer Service
Closure enter notes and resolution code capture structured action, blocker, result, and unresolved reason Service Operations Manager
Quality and improvement sample contacts and review complaints aggregate repeat-contact and upstream failure patterns Service Quality Lead and Journey Process Owner

The project's process boundary starts when a relevant contact or stalled case is identified. It ends when the customer receives a resolution or explicit next step and the result is recorded. Upstream process redesign discovered through the pilot becomes a separate improvement backlog owned by the journey process owner.

Journey Process Owner definition work

The Journey Process Owner makes the common proposal specific enough to operate. They must:

  • define the journey start, completion, and unresolved states;
  • define when separate contacts belong to the same customer need;
  • map the current process, decision points, queues, ownership changes, and customer communications;
  • identify the common blockers and evidence used to recognize them;
  • approve the actions available to the service employee for each relevant state;
  • define exceptions, specialist referrals, complaints, vulnerability, fraud, and other escalation conditions;
  • define what constitutes resolution, a committed next step, an unsuccessful resolution attempt, and a reopened case;
  • approve the structured status, blocker, action, and outcome language used by the project;
  • review historical cases and confirm the correct interpretation and next action;
  • own the upstream process-improvement backlog revealed by recurring failure patterns.

The current and target process maps, action catalogue, exception map, and outcome definitions are the Process Owner's formal inputs to the project.

Execution rule

Each step must leave an owned reusable asset. The historical case set becomes evaluation data. The taxonomy becomes a common service language. The linked timeline becomes a customer-context component. The employee view becomes a reusable interaction design. The outcome record becomes the learning loop.

Project Manager initiation responsibilities

The Project Manager converts this use-case definition into the bank's project-initiation form. At minimum, they:

  • record the selected journey, team, cohort, scope, exclusions, sponsor, Process Owner, and workstream owners;
  • establish the benefit baseline, planning targets, metric definitions, evidence-sizing approach, measurement sources, Benefit Owner, and Measurement Owner;
  • ensure each customer-protection and control limit has a source, owner, tolerance, review frequency, and suspension threshold before live use;
  • confirm named participants and capacity for service, process, data, quality, control, and delivery work;
  • turn the delivery action workflow into an integrated plan and dependency map;
  • maintain the project backlog, RAID log, decision log, change control, and approval evidence;
  • establish the governance forum, reporting path, escalation route, and decision cadence;
  • coordinate historical-case readiness, employee readiness, control review, and live-use readiness;
  • ensure training, operating instructions, fallback, support, and outcome monitoring are ready before live use;
  • prepare the evidence and recommendation for scale, redesign, reuse, or closure;
  • confirm continuing ownership for every capability and process change produced by the project.

The Project Manager owns coordination and evidence completeness. The Sponsor owns the investment decision, the Journey Process Owner owns process correctness, and the Service Owner owns the customer outcome.

Project controls

  • One approved pilot charter defines the journey, cohort, customer outcome, scope boundary, owners, baseline, and acceptance criteria.
  • One integrated backlog connects process, data, technology, control, adoption, and measurement work.
  • A dependency and decision log records source access, policy interpretation, process exceptions, integration, and readiness decisions.
  • Historical-case validation precedes employee use. Employee use with full review precedes customer-visible intervention.
  • Live quality and customer-outcome review can suspend the affected feature immediately.
  • Scale requires continuing business, process, data, technology, support, and control ownership.

Operational workflow for each customer case

Actions available to the employee

The selected journey defines a short approved action list. Typical actions are:

  • explain current status and the reason for delay;
  • complete an outstanding internal service step;
  • request specific missing information once;
  • correct routing or ownership;
  • create a callback or specialist referral with full context;
  • provide a clear committed next step and expected service state;
  • escalate a complaint, vulnerability, fraud, or other specialist condition.

The use case recommends from this approved list. It does not invent process steps.

Initial risk position

The pilot is an employee-assistance capability within an existing customer-service process:

  • The employee remains accountable for interpretation, communication, and action.
  • Every customer communication and operational action receives employee approval.
  • The capability uses approved service records and authoritative journey knowledge for the selected purpose.
  • Recommendations are limited to actions approved by the Journey Process Owner.
  • Low-confidence or conflicting evidence routes the case to the existing investigation process.
  • Inferred blockers remain reviewable working hypotheses. They do not become permanent customer facts.
  • Credit, eligibility, pricing, fraud, AML, sanctions, suitability, or other regulated decisions remain outside scope.
  • The existing customer complaint, correction, escalation, and human-service routes remain available.

This position is confirmed against the bank's AI risk classification and local regulatory obligations before live employee use.

Risk, Compliance, Conduct, and Privacy coverage

Area Question the project must resolve Required evidence or decision
Purpose and lawful use May the selected records be combined and analyzed for service resolution? documented purpose, legal basis, permitted-use decision, and data owners
Data minimization Which fields and history are necessary for this journey? approved field/source list and exclusions
Access and confidentiality Which employees may see the assembled customer context? role definition, need-to-know rule, and access-review owner
Vulnerability and sensitive information How are vulnerability indicators and sensitive case content handled? display, suppression, escalation, and handling rules
Accuracy and customer treatment What happens when history is incomplete, conflicting, or incorrectly linked? confidence rules, employee verification, correction, and manual fallback
Fairness and conduct Could customers or cohorts receive poorer service from classification or routing? cohort monitoring, complaint review, and prohibited treatment rules
Customer communication What may be communicated, and is AI transparency required? approved communication approach, reviewer responsibility, and disclosure decision
Records and traceability What must be retained to reconstruct a recommendation and action? required audit fields, retention owner, and record location
Incident and suspension Which events stop the pilot or require escalation? incident triggers, notification route, stop authority, and restart decision
Risk classification How is the implemented use classified under bank policy and applicable law? recorded classification, rationale, reviewer, and material-change triggers

The relevant control functions review their areas before controlled live use. Their role is to confirm the operating limits and evidence requirements. The Journey Process Owner and Service Owner remain accountable for the business process and customer outcome.

Pilot acceptance

  • The selected primary customer outcome and operational benefit meet the targets recorded in the project-initiation record, or provide sufficient directional evidence for the Sponsor's stated next decision.
  • Historical validation satisfies the approved coverage plan for common states, blockers, and material exceptions; 200–500 manually reviewed cases is the normal planning range for one defined journey scope.
  • Live workflow evidence covers a representative employee group and enough eligible cases to expose usability, correction, training, and operational failure modes; at least 100 cases is the normal planning minimum.
  • Customer-outcome evidence meets the post-baseline sample and comparison design required for the claimed decision. High-volume journeys may need approximately 1,000–3,000 eligible cases in each pilot and comparison population; lower-volume journeys record why directional evidence is sufficient for a limited next step.
  • At least 80% of reviewed summaries and proposed next steps are accepted as useful by service experts.
  • Every displayed fact and status can be traced to a source record.
  • Unsupported or low-confidence conclusions are withheld or clearly marked for investigation.
  • Investigation or handling effort improves against the agreed baseline.
  • Repeat contact, unnecessary handoff, unresolved-case age, or rework improves without deterioration in complaints or customer outcomes.
  • Every employee correction, accepted action, escalation, and result is recorded.
  • No critical privacy, access, security, or customer-treatment incident occurs.

The charter records eligibility and exclusions, metric formulas and denominators, comparison method, observation period, state and exception coverage, and treatment of reopened, transferred, abandoned, and incomplete cases. Statistical significance is claimed only when the Measurement Owner confirms that volume and cohort construction support it.

Scope boundary

The pilot does not require a general customer 360, customer chatbot, autonomous customer action, transaction intelligence, or enterprise-wide knowledge base. It uses the minimum sources and procedures needed for one service journey.

The business problem, process, ownership, benefit, risk position, and initiation requirements are agreed before detailed solution architecture, platform selection, delivery service levels, and formal IT commitment.

Reuse after validation

The same delivery model can be extended to another service journey by replacing its taxonomy, source mappings, approved actions, and evaluation cases. The reusable core is:

  • customer interaction timeline;
  • service intent and unresolved-state model;
  • evidence-linked employee view;
  • governed service knowledge retrieval;
  • correction and outcome feedback;
  • controlled analysis and audit path.
Project charters

Customer Intelligence–Enabled Service Resolution — Candidate Project Charters

Customer Intelligence–Enabled Service Resolution offers three selectable project charters. One customer journey is selected, its ownership and baseline fields are completed, its proposed targets are confirmed, and it enters the bank's normal project-initiation process.

The Technical Pilot Blueprint defines the common banking-systems, customer-intelligence, GenAI, and agentic solution used to implement the selected charter.

The journey technical profiles define the systems, context, knowledge, AI-assistant functions, tools, control boundaries, and validation expected for each candidate. The platform capability and readiness map defines what IT must assess and provide without assuming a particular bank product or runtime.

Charter approval authorizes mobilization, baseline work, control definition, and pilot preparation. Controlled live use remains a separate readiness decision, and pilot approval does not authorize broader rollout.

Candidate charter Best fit Primary customer outcome Relative complexity
Payment Issue Resolution high payment-contact volume and fragmented payment status fewer repeat contacts and faster confirmed resolution lower
Card Dispute Progress Support repeated status calls and evidence confusion during disputes clearer progress and fewer avoidable status contacts medium
Onboarding/KYC Progress Support stalled applications and repeated information requests faster progression with one clear request for valid information medium–high

Selection rule

Select the journey with:

  • material repeat-contact or stalled-case volume;
  • one accountable process owner;
  • a stable existing resolution process;
  • accessible case and contact records;
  • a measurable customer outcome;
  • a service team able to operate the controlled pilot.

Common acceptance logic

Each candidate charter uses five measure groups:

  1. Customer outcome: the journey-specific problem improves against baseline.
  2. Operational benefit: investigation, handling, handoff, or rework improves.
  3. Adoption and acceptance: employees use the capability and judge it useful.
  4. Quality: facts, statuses, blockers, and actions are supported and sufficiently accurate.
  5. Customer protection and control limits: complaints, customer treatment, privacy, and control outcomes remain within agreed limits.

Proposed targets are starting thresholds. The Sponsor, Journey Process Owner, Service Quality Lead, and relevant control functions confirm or replace them after the baseline is established and before controlled live use.

The project passes only when all mandatory quality and control-limit criteria pass and the primary outcome provides sufficient evidence for the Sponsor's stated scale decision.

Minimum evidence expectation

The charter sizes evidence according to the question being answered:

Evidence purpose Realistic planning expectation Why it is needed
Historical quality and failure analysis normally 200–500 manually reviewed cases for one defined journey scope, with deliberate coverage of every common state, blocker, and material exception demonstrates that the timeline, status, blocker, and proposed action are correct across the journey; raw volume cannot replace state and exception coverage
Live workflow and employee acceptance normally at least 100 eligible cases across a representative group of service employees exposes workflow friction, correction behavior, training needs, adoption, and operational failure modes
Customer-outcome evidence calculated from the baseline outcome rate, target improvement, eligible volume, and required confidence; high-volume journeys may require roughly 1,000–3,000 cases in each pilot/comparison population repeat contact and progression are binary or time-based outcomes; a small usability sample cannot reliably demonstrate a modest business improvement

For illustration, reducing a 30% repeat-contact rate by 15% relatively means moving it to 25.5%, an absolute change of 4.5 percentage points. Demonstrating that difference reliably commonly requires well over 1,000 eligible cases in each comparison population. The Measurement Owner calculates the actual requirement after baseline. Lower-volume journeys may use a longer observation period, a larger relative target, or directional outcome evidence with an explicitly limited scale decision.

The charter records:

  • eligibility and exclusion rules;
  • metric formula and denominator;
  • baseline and comparison design;
  • outcome observation period;
  • required coverage of process states and material exceptions;
  • minimum live-workflow sample;
  • customer-outcome sample or directional-evidence rationale;
  • treatment of reopened, transferred, abandoned, and incomplete cases.

These ranges are planning expectations rather than quotas. Common categories need enough reviewed examples to reveal recurring performance, while rare high-severity exceptions may require review of every available case. Coverage and the decision to be supported take precedence over an arbitrary total.

Control-limit expectation

Before live use, every charter names each control-limit metric, source, owner, tolerance, review frequency, and suspension threshold. Zero-tolerance events are stated separately from monitored non-inferiority measures.

Typical zero-tolerance events include missed legal or scheme deadlines caused by the capability, loss of customer rights, unauthorized disclosure, an unreviewed customer communication, bypass of a mandatory control, and critical customer harm. Complaints, corrections, customer satisfaction, unresolved-case age, accessibility, and vulnerable-customer outcomes use baseline-informed tolerances.

Evidence and control-limit schedule required before live use

The completed charter records eligibility and exclusions, metric formulas and denominators, baseline/comparison design, observation period, state and exception coverage, live-workflow sample, and outcome sample or directional-evidence rationale. Each control limit records its metric, source, owner, baseline-informed tolerance, review frequency, and suspension threshold.

Acceptance rule

The Sponsor may approve scale when the primary customer outcome and one operational benefit meet their confirmed targets, all mandatory quality and control-limit criteria pass, Payments Operations accepts the interpretation and action workflow, and the Measurement Owner confirms that the evidence supports that decision.

Directional evidence may authorize only a defined extension or further measurement. Refine applies when quality and controls pass but benefit evidence is inconclusive. Stop applies when payment state cannot be established reliably, the workflow creates material additional effort, or a control limit cannot be maintained.

Risk, compliance, conduct, and privacy position

  • Employee-assistive use remains within the existing Payments servicing process; the employee verifies the evidence and owns the response.
  • Payment status and next step remain grounded in authoritative records and actions approved by the Journey Process Owner.
  • The approved purpose and minimum necessary data fields are recorded before use.
  • Customer communication, transparency, accessibility, and vulnerable-customer handling follow approved service rules.
  • Recommendations, source evidence, employee decisions, corrections, and outcomes are traceable and retained under an approved rule.
  • Incidents, suspension authority, restart approval, and material-change triggers are agreed before live use.
  • Fraud, disputes, AML, sanctions, authorization, reimbursement, compensation, and funds movement remain in their existing governed processes.
  • Conflicting or incomplete payment records route to manual investigation.

IT architecture

Customer Intelligence–Enabled Service Resolution — Technical Pilot Blueprint

Technical proposition

The bank implements one controlled service-resolution journey across authoritative banking systems, purpose-bound customer context, governed GenAI interpretation, employee-approved action, and measured customer outcome.

The business proposal and delivery model fixes the customer outcome, ownership and operating boundary. A common technical architecture supplies customer context, approved knowledge, AI-assisted workflow, policy enforcement, evidence and the route to shared platform capabilities. The journey technical profiles apply the specific system, information and action boundaries for Payment Issue Resolution, Card Dispute Progress Support, and Onboarding/KYC Progress Support. The platform capability and readiness map determines which bank capabilities can be reused, extended, supplied locally or must narrow the pilot.

The recommended first implementation is a Payment Issue Resolution Workspace supported by a Limited-Authority Service Resolution Assistant. Payment issue resolution provides a relatively clear authoritative state, material service volume, measurable repeat contact, and a controlled decision boundary. The same architecture can later be configured for disputes, onboarding/KYC progress, and other service journeys with their respective information and action limits.

Executive visual — from banking facts to reusable platform

The pilot creates customer value on the solid line. The dotted lines show which assets can become shared platform capabilities after reuse is demonstrated.

What the pilot must demonstrate

The technical pilot must demonstrate that the bank can:

  1. assemble an authorized, source-linked view of one customer-service problem from several banking systems;
  2. use GenAI to interpret fragmented interaction history and approved knowledge more effectively than the existing workflow and a data-only alternative;
  3. constrain the AI assistant to a defined workflow, approved tools, and explicit employee decision points;
  4. deliver a customer-visible service benefit through the existing servicing process;
  5. replay the complete path from source records through model interpretation, employee action, and customer outcome;
  6. retain reusable customer-context, knowledge, evaluation, tool, control, and outcome components for later journeys.

Where GenAI adds value

GenAI is applied to work that is difficult to express as stable deterministic rules:

  • interpret fragmented contact notes, chats, cases, and complaints;
  • reconstruct a concise customer-issue timeline;
  • distinguish the current need from earlier related requests;
  • identify and explain a likely unresolved-service blocker;
  • retrieve and apply the relevant approved procedure;
  • propose a permitted next service action;
  • create a clear, source-grounded explanation for employee review.

GenAI does not establish customer identity, payment status, eligibility, deadlines, permissions, or transaction outcome. Those remain facts and decisions supplied by authoritative banking systems and approved policy.

Target pilot architecture

The architecture separates five responsibilities:

  1. Banking systems provide authoritative facts and execute governed banking processes.
  2. The Customer Context Service creates the minimum authorized view required for this journey.
  3. The Service Resolution Assistant interprets the context and knowledge within a controlled, limited-authority workflow.
  4. The Service Resolution Workspace keeps the employee accountable for communication and action.
  5. The evidence and outcome path demonstrates benefit and contributes reusable Customer Intelligence.

Enterprise placement and pilot isolation

The pilot is isolated operationally but integrated architecturally. It receives a dedicated workload identity, data purpose, deployment boundary, source allow-list, knowledge corpus, tool allow-list, evaluation set, telemetry stream, and suspension control. It integrates through bank-owned contracts that can survive replacement of the pilot implementation.

This avoids two opposite risks: coupling an experiment directly to core systems, and producing a disconnected demonstration that cannot enter normal service.

The enterprise boundary is:

Service Resolution journey application
  consumes limited-authority AI-assistant and shared AI platform capabilities
  consumes purpose-bound Customer Intelligence context
  invokes registered banking APIs and workflows

AI and agentic platforms
  provide model, retrieval, orchestration, policy, tool and evidence primitives
  do not own journey logic, customer facts or regulated banking decisions

Banking, data and identity platforms
  remain systems of record and enterprise trust roots

Capability-layer view

Layer Enterprise role What the pilot consumes or establishes
Journey solution employee experience and service resolution workflow Service Resolution Workspace, journey eligibility, process state, action catalogue and outcome capture
Minimum Customer Intelligence capability purpose-bound customer understanding identity linkage, normalized service-event timeline, context snapshot, inference separation and outcome history
Agentic workflow platform controlled orchestration and tool use workflow state, registered tools, delegated authority, checkpoints, budgets and execution trace
AI platform safe reusable AI capabilities model gateway, governed knowledge retrieval, prompt/model registry, evaluation, AI safety controls and observability
Model serving foundation-model inference as a service an approved managed provider or an existing/new in-bank inference endpoint
Compute and data substrate execution environment application compute, data services, container runtime, network, storage and GPU capacity only where model serving requires it
Enterprise controls and shared services enterprise trust and information identity, secrets, API management, data platform, security operations, records and service management

The pilot may implement a missing capability locally behind the target interface. A local component becomes a shared platform capability only when it has another committed consumer, a named product owner, independent service expectations, funding, support, and a lifecycle. This enables validation without prematurely creating a large platform estate.

Integration principles

  • Use versioned service and event contracts so model, agent framework, UI, and source adapters can be replaced independently.
  • Keep journey-specific process interpretation in the service resolution solution; extract only genuinely reusable capabilities into platforms.
  • Access core systems through existing APIs or controlled façades. Use event streams or CDC for history and outcome propagation where supported.
  • Use governed snapshots for historical development and evaluation, not as an unmonitored live source of truth.
  • Avoid direct model access to core databases, production credentials, message buses, or unrestricted enterprise search.
  • Preserve authoritative source references through context assembly, model interpretation, employee action, and outcome reporting.

Banking systems and information required

Every journey uses the following banking capability set. The actual systems, fields, interfaces, and restrictions are completed in the selected journey technical profile.

Banking capability Information used Authority retained by the banking capability
Customer master or CRM customer identity, servicing relationship, segment and relevant preferences customer identity and relationship record
Selected journey system journey identifier, business object, timestamps, authoritative status and approved state/reason codes payment, dispute, onboarding or other journey state
Case or workflow system investigation state, responsible queue, outstanding step, actions and resolution operational case state and process execution
Contact platforms previous contacts, contact reasons, messages or permitted transcripts source interaction record
Complaints system complaint, escalation and resolution state formal complaint record and obligations
Knowledge repositories approved procedures, explanations, routing and escalation rules authoritative service knowledge
Identity and access services employee identity, role, entitlements and customer relationship authentication and authorization
Management information and outcome sources subsequent contact, handling effort, resolution, complaint and reopen official benefit and control reporting

Only fields required for the selected journey and service resolution workflow are provided. The model receives purpose-bound context through controlled services rather than unrestricted access to core systems.

Integration approach

The pilot uses two information paths:

  • Historical evaluation path: governed extracts from the relevant systems are normalized into reviewed historical cases for development, evaluation, and baseline measurement.
  • Live servicing path: controlled read APIs or adapters retrieve current authoritative state when an eligible case is opened. Event feeds may supply recent contacts and outcome changes where they already exist.

Every value provided to the workspace carries a source reference and freshness timestamp. Missing, stale, conflicting, or incorrectly linked information is surfaced as an exception and follows the existing manual investigation route.

Purpose-bound Customer Context Service

The Customer Context Service is the first concrete Customer Intelligence component. It:

  • links the customer, selected journey event or application, open case, and related contacts using stable bank identifiers;
  • normalizes records into a common service-event timeline;
  • distinguishes authoritative facts, calculated values, and GenAI inferences;
  • applies purpose, role, field, and retention restrictions;
  • provides source, timestamp, freshness, and ownership metadata;
  • produces a reproducible context snapshot for every model interpretation and employee action;
  • publishes the recorded action and outcome back into the customer-service event history.

For the pilot, this is a journey-specific context service rather than an enterprise customer 360. Its identity, event, provenance, and outcome contracts should be designed for reuse by later customer-intelligence journeys.

Minimum event structure

Each normalized service event should contain:

event identifier
customer and journey identifiers
source system and source record
event type and business timestamp
authoritative status or approved reason code
responsible process owner or queue
purpose and access classification
freshness and ingestion timestamp

Inferences are stored separately with their evidence, model and prompt version, confidence, purpose, and expiry. They do not become authoritative customer facts.

Limited-Authority Service Resolution Assistant

The Service Resolution Assistant is implemented as a controlled workflow rather than an open-ended autonomous loop.

The workflow controller enforces:

  • a fixed sequence and maximum number of steps;
  • an allow-listed set of read and write tools;
  • structured request and response schemas;
  • per-case time, model-call, and cost limits;
  • source and citation validation;
  • explicit separation of facts and inferences;
  • abstention when evidence is insufficient or conflicting;
  • a manual fallback at every material failure point;
  • employee approval before customer communication or operational action.

The pilot uses request-scoped workflow state. Durable customer memory belongs to the governed Customer Intelligence layer rather than free-form agent memory.

Software and agentic realization

The architectural requirement is a durable, observable state machine with typed tools and policy checkpoints. The implementation may use an established workflow engine combined with an agent framework, or an agent framework that supplies equivalent durable execution. Framework choice is subordinate to the following contracts:

  • explicit workflow states and transitions rather than an unrestricted reasoning loop;
  • structured model outputs validated against versioned schemas;
  • resumable execution around employee approval and external-system latency;
  • deterministic retry, timeout, idempotency and compensation behavior;
  • model, prompt, retrieval, tool and policy versions attached to the case trace;
  • replay of historical trajectories against a changed component;
  • framework-independent tool and context interfaces.

The recommended software split is:

Concern Architectural choice for the pilot
durable execution a bank-supported workflow/state-machine runtime owns pauses, employee approval, retry, timeout and recovery
LLM orchestration a lightweight orchestration component operates inside defined workflow states and communicates only through the model gateway and registered tools
customer context a separate typed service supplies authorized facts and snapshots; it is not agent memory
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) a separate retrieval service indexes approved journey knowledge, applies access/effective-date filters and returns citations
tools versioned bank API contracts are canonical; an MCP adapter is optional at the agent boundary
authorization the bank policy service and tool broker decide access and action authority; the agent framework does not
evaluation a framework-independent harness replays the same cases across model, prompt, RAG and orchestrator changes
observability enterprise telemetry receives a common execution-trace schema independent of the chosen orchestration library

The main functional services compose as follows:

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is used for approved procedures and communication guidance. Customer facts are obtained from the Customer Context Service rather than a vector index. Retrieval must inherit document access, effective dates, ownership and withdrawal state, and the generated output must cite the retrieved source.

MCP may be used as a tool-description and invocation adapter when it fits the bank's engineering standards. It is not the authorization boundary. The bank's tool broker still owns workload identity, delegated employee/customer context, policy, credentials, confirmation, rate limits and audit. Direct MCP connections from a model or desktop to core banking systems are outside the target architecture.

Multi-agent collaboration and A2A are unnecessary for the first service resolution journey. Separate specialist agents should be introduced only when an independently owned capability has a distinct context, tool authority, lifecycle and evaluation requirement. The initial workflow is clearer and safer as one orchestrator calling deterministic services and limited model functions.

Registered tools and authority

The initial tool catalogue can contain:

Tool Authority Pilot use
get_customer_service_context read retrieve the authorized customer and journey context
get_journey_status read obtain the current authoritative state permitted by the selected journey profile
get_related_contacts read retrieve permitted related contacts and prior communication
get_open_case read obtain case stage, owner and outstanding service step
get_applicable_procedure read retrieve effective approved procedure and communication guidance
get_permitted_actions read return actions approved for the verified process state
record_employee_feedback constrained write record acceptance, correction, rejection or escalation reason
create_specialist_referral constrained write with employee approval open or update an existing governed referral workflow
draft_case_note draft only produce a structured note for employee review
record_service_outcome constrained write record the resulting service state and measurement event

The pilot does not expose tools that move or reverse money, change an authoritative journey state, make a regulated decision, determine reimbursement, alter fraud/AML/sanctions state, or send an unreviewed customer message. Each journey profile adds its more restrictive exclusions.

For every tool call, the tool broker verifies workload and employee identity, customer context, declared purpose, scope, input constraints, required confirmation, and audit obligations. Write operations use the existing system's validation, idempotency, authorization, and recordkeeping controls.

Service Resolution Workspace

The employee experience should be a side panel within, or closely coupled to, the existing service desktop. It presents:

  1. Customer request — the need currently being handled.
  2. What happened — a concise evidence-linked timeline.
  3. Verified current state — from the authoritative journey system.
  4. Likely blocker — visibly marked as an inference with its evidence.
  5. Applicable procedure — effective approved source and relevant section.
  6. Permitted next step — selected from the Journey Process Owner's action catalogue.
  7. Suggested customer explanation — grounded draft for employee approval.
  8. Source evidence — deep links to the underlying records.
  9. Employee decision — accept, correct, reject, investigate, or escalate.

The workspace should avoid an unconstrained general-chat experience. The task-oriented view makes the source evidence, action boundary, corrections, and customer outcome observable.

Minimum Reusable AI and Controlled-Workflow Foundation

The pilot requires a limited shared technical path:

Capability Pilot implementation Reusable result
Model gateway authenticated approved model route, allow-list, limits and usage attribution provider-independent bank model interface
Model and prompt registry versioned model, system instructions, prompt templates and output schemas reproducible AI configuration
Governed retrieval access-aware index of approved journey procedures with freshness and citation reusable banking-knowledge service design
Evaluation service historical datasets, expected results, policy tests, adversarial cases and regression gates repeatable release evidence
AI safety controls restricted-data, content, citation, schema, action and customer-communication validation reusable controls enforced during each request
Service Resolution Workflow controlled workflow state, retries, timeouts, budgets and fallback reusable limited-authority assistant runtime
Tool broker registered tools, delegated identity, scoped authority, approval and audit governed interface to banking actions
Observability full case execution path, retrieval, policy, model, tool, latency, error and cost trace incident replay and operational evidence
Use-case registry purpose, owners, sources, model, knowledge, tools, risk tier and approvals current AI service inventory
Suspension controls disable generation, a specific tool, model route, or complete service reusable operational suspension mechanism

Existing enterprise model providers, search, IAM, logging, deployment, security-monitoring, and data-platform capabilities should be reused where fit. The bank must own the customer-context contract, banking adapters, action catalogue, policy rules, evaluation cases, knowledge authority, tool contracts, and outcome definitions.

The gateway contract should permit either an approved managed model or an in-bank model-serving endpoint. A broader on-prem LLM infrastructure programme is therefore an explicit dependency choice rather than a prerequisite embedded into this pilot.

Deployment and infrastructure position

Agents do not inherently require GPU infrastructure. GPU demand comes from embedding, reranking, and foundation-model inference choices. The workspace, orchestrator, tool broker, context service, policy enforcement, evaluation control plane, and most integration services run on normal application compute.

Three deployment positions are viable:

Position Pilot infrastructure implication Long-term implication
Approved managed model through the bank gateway no dedicated inference GPU; deploy application and data services in the bank environment and enforce approved network/egress routes fastest validation while retaining provider portability through the gateway
Existing internal model-serving platform consume its authenticated endpoint and declared service levels validates whether the current platform meets quality, latency, capacity and control needs
New on-prem model serving provide a separate L1 inference service with GPU scheduling, model registry, scaling and support justified only where data, residency, economics, latency or strategic control require it

For a new on-prem path, hardware cannot be responsibly selected from the word “agent.” Capacity depends on model size and quantization, context length, tokens generated, concurrent cases, latency objective, availability design, embedding/reranking load, and growth reserve. A single inference node may support laboratory evaluation. Controlled live service normally requires failure isolation and redundant serving capacity. High-bandwidth GPU interconnect is needed only when the selected model or throughput profile spans several GPUs; it is not a general requirement of agent orchestration.

The pilot therefore supplies Infra and SRE with measured request rate, token profile, concurrency, latency, storage, retention, and availability observations before a scale hardware commitment.

Operational and SRE expectations

  • separate development, evaluation, and controlled-live environments;
  • infrastructure as code, secrets management and workload identity;
  • dependency health for banking APIs, gateway, model, retrieval, policy and tool broker;
  • end-to-end correlation from employee request to source reads, model calls, tool actions and outcome;
  • service-level indicators for availability, latency, error, fallback, queue age and cost;
  • graceful degradation to context-only or existing manual service when AI dependencies fail;
  • progressive release, rollback, model-route failover and tested suspension controls;
  • capacity, cost and incident ownership for every shared component.

Engineering, CI/CD and test strategy

Application code, infrastructure, prompts, schemas, policies, retrieval configuration, knowledge versions and evaluation datasets are versioned release inputs. The delivery pipeline should run the appropriate evidence for each change:

Test layer Required acceptance evidence
Software unit and component deterministic rules, schemas, redaction, policy and workflow transitions behave correctly
API and contract source, context, tool and outcome contracts remain compatible and enforce authorization
Data quality identifiers, status mappings, completeness, freshness, exclusions and quarantine rules pass
Retrieval correct effective source is returned; stale, conflicting, restricted and irrelevant sources are handled
Model evaluation factual support, case interpretation, next-step quality, abstention and communication quality meet the charter threshold
Agent execution path allowed paths, maximum steps, approvals, retries, timeouts, duplicate prevention and tool denial behave correctly
Security and adversarial prompt injection, data exfiltration, cross-customer access, malicious documents and tool manipulation are resisted
Resilience and performance dependency failure, degraded mode, recovery, capacity, latency and suspension operate as designed
Business acceptance service SMEs validate representative states and exceptions; employees can correct and use the result

Release progression is blocked by failed mandatory evaluation or policy tests. Controlled-live deployment uses a small eligible cohort, observable feature flags, and component-level rollback. A changed model, prompt, retrieval corpus, status mapping, tool, policy or workflow runs through its defined regression scope before promotion.

Data and evaluation assets

The Data and Test Strategy teams provide three deliberately separated assets:

  1. Development cases for exploration, taxonomy and workflow refinement.
  2. Locked acceptance cases unseen during development and owned by the Measurement Owner and Journey Process Owner.
  3. Live monitoring samples drawn from eligible production cases under the approved purpose and review process.

Historical cases should be pseudonymized or consistently tokenized across source systems so that customer, journey event or application, contact and case relationships remain realistic while direct identifiers are removed. Dates and values may be shifted or transformed only where process order, state transitions, thresholds and exception behavior remain valid. Synthetic cases can extend rare and adversarial coverage but do not replace real representative cases for benefit or operational acceptance.

Each accepted case records the source state, expected interpretation, permitted action, relevant procedure, material exclusions and SME rationale. Access to any re-identification mapping remains outside the model and ordinary development environment.

IT contribution and dependency map

Each contributing team should be asked for a named owner, agreed interface or deliverable, supported environment, service expectation, constraint, and fallback. The project should avoid asking platform teams for an undefined “AI environment” or unrestricted source access.

AI Policy and Security Enforcement

The AI policy and enforcement layer is distributed through explicit policy decision and enforcement points:

Security and compliance depend on the following capabilities rather than on prompt instructions alone:

  • workload identity and employee/customer delegation propagated end to end;
  • least-privilege source and tool access with short-lived credentials;
  • field-level minimization before model invocation;
  • encrypted transport and storage with approved residency and retention;
  • provider terms and configuration preventing bank data from being used for model training;
  • protection against instructions embedded in contacts, documents or retrieved knowledge;
  • separation of retrieved content from system instructions and tool authority;
  • output schema, source, sensitive-data and prohibited-action validation;
  • immutable or protected decision and action evidence with privacy-aware content logging;
  • cross-customer isolation tests, access review, incident route and service suspension controls.

The policy service returns an enforceable decision and reason. The context service, AI gateway, retrieval service, orchestrator, tool broker and communication path enforce that decision and emit evidence. This is the pilot realization of the bank's wider AI policy layer.

How the pilot isolates GenAI benefit

A simple before-and-after comparison would combine several effects and would not show whether GenAI itself created value. The pilot should compare three operating modes:

Mode Employee receives Question answered
Existing process current systems and procedures what is the business baseline?
Context-only workspace linked facts, deterministic timeline and source links without generated interpretation how much benefit comes from data consolidation?
GenAI-assisted workspace context plus summary, blocker interpretation, retrieved procedure, proposed next step and explanation what incremental benefit comes from GenAI?

The comparison begins with blinded historical evaluation, proceeds through silent evaluation alongside the existing process without influencing customers, and then uses controlled live populations where operationally feasible.

Measures are separated by component:

  • time required to understand the case;
  • correctness of current-state interpretation;
  • correctness of the selected next step;
  • unsupported or materially misleading statements;
  • employee corrections and rejected recommendations;
  • handling and investigation effort;
  • repeat contact and case progression;
  • customer complaints and adverse outcomes;
  • technical availability, latency, failures and fallback;
  • cost per processed case and per successfully resolved case.

If the context-only workspace produces most of the improvement, the result supports investment in customer-context integration while limiting additional GenAI investment. GenAI is justified by measurable incremental improvement in interpretation, knowledge use, explanation quality, employee effort, or adaptability to additional journeys.

Technical validation progression

The solution increases exposure only after the preceding behavior is demonstrated:

  1. Historical case reconstruction and blinded SME evaluation.
  2. Customer Context Service and deterministic timeline.
  3. Governed knowledge retrieval.
  4. Structured GenAI interpretation and proposed action.
  5. Evidence validation, policy tests, and regression gates.
  6. Employee workspace in silent evaluation alongside the existing process.
  7. Controlled live employee assistance.
  8. Employee-approved customer communication through an existing channel.
  9. Authenticated read-only customer self-service after service-state and explanation quality are established.
  10. Limited-authority customer actions only after separate tool, policy, authentication, and customer-confirmation approval.

This progression separates permission to mobilize and build from permission to use live customer information, influence communication, or execute an action.

Technical validation criteria

The completed pilot should demonstrate:

  • correct customer, journey object or event, and case linkage or explicit quarantine;
  • authoritative status never replaced by model inference;
  • facts, calculations, and inferences remain visibly distinct;
  • every material displayed fact and proposed action links to its source and version;
  • no prohibited tool or action can be invoked through the AI-assisted workflow;
  • low-confidence, stale, conflicting, and unavailable-source conditions use the manual fallback;
  • historical and live evaluations can be rerun against a new model, prompt, knowledge, or policy version;
  • every live case can be replayed from source context through employee decision and outcome;
  • model, retrieval, orchestration, and tool failures can be isolated and suspended;
  • the GenAI-assisted mode provides measurable incremental value over the context-only mode;
  • cost and operational performance are compatible with the intended service workflow;
  • components produced by the pilot have named continuing technical and business owners.

Journey-specific numerical thresholds remain in the approved project charter and its evidence-and-control-limit schedule.

Pilot-to-platform evolution

The pilot is designed to become the first consumer and proving ground of a shared platform, while keeping the journey solution replaceable. Scale occurs by extracting stable, reused capabilities rather than expanding the pilot application into an enterprise monolith.

Evolution state What operates Investment decision
Controlled evaluation environment historical data, context assembly, knowledge retrieval, model evaluation and workflow simulation confirm technical quality and viable source integration
First controlled production journey one journey application on controlled shared model, policy, evidence and tool paths demonstrate customer outcome, operational fit, control and unit cost
Reusable implementation path a second and third journey consume standard gateway, knowledge-retrieval, evaluation, orchestration, context and tool contracts fund shared capabilities with owners, service levels, support and product roadmaps
Enterprise AI and Agentic Workflow Platform multi-team self-service onboarding, control profiles, registries, reusable tool catalogue, observability and economics operate shared AI delivery as a platform product
Customer Intelligence and Action Platform reusable identity, event, feature, context, decision and outcome services support channels and agents scale from service resolution into broader contextual banking and customer self-sufficiency

What is adopted as a shared capability

Pilot asset Platform destination
model route, prompt versions and usage evidence AI gateway and model/prompt registry
journey knowledge corpus and retrieval tests governed knowledge-retrieval service
historical cases and regression pipeline enterprise AI evaluation capability
controlled workflow and execution trace controlled-workflow runtime and supported implementation path
registered read/write tools and authorization design banking tool broker and reusable tool catalogue
context snapshot and normalized service events Customer Intelligence context and event interfaces
policy decisions and enforcement evidence reusable AI use-case control profile and policy service
workspace interaction and correction design employee-assist design system or channel component
action and outcome events enterprise measurement and Customer Intelligence learning loop

What the future platform covers

The resulting platform gives delivery teams a supported way to:

  • register and classify an AI-enabled journey;
  • obtain an approved model route;
  • connect governed knowledge and purpose-bound context;
  • build and evaluate a limited-authority assistant workflow;
  • invoke banking tools with scoped delegated authority;
  • inherit security, policy, evidence, deployment and monitoring controls;
  • measure quality, cost and customer outcome;
  • change models or frameworks without rewriting the banking integration.

It does not replace core banking systems, enterprise IAM, API management, the data platform, business workflow systems, regulated decision engines, or journey ownership. It composes those capabilities into a safe AI delivery path.

CTO scale decision

At the end of the pilot, the CTO should receive a capability assessment rather than only a use-case demonstration:

  • which existing enterprise capabilities were successfully reused;
  • which local pilot components should remain journey-specific;
  • which components have a committed second consumer and should become shared platform capabilities;
  • quality, latency, resilience, security and unit-cost evidence for each layer;
  • vendor and framework dependencies, portability and exit constraints;
  • source-system and API gaps that limit additional journeys;
  • the proposed platform product owners, service expectations, operating cost and investment sequence.

This makes the scale decision explicit: reuse the first end-to-end journey, adopt validated shared capabilities, replace temporary components behind stable contracts, and retire pilot-only infrastructure when its function is available on the supported implementation path.

Reusable outcome and strategic fit

The pilot produces more than a single assistant:

  • the first purpose-bound customer-context interface;
  • a common customer-service event model;
  • a governed journey-knowledge product;
  • bank-owned historical evaluation and regression cases;
  • a controlled model and prompt route;
  • a limited-authority assistant-orchestration design;
  • a delegated banking-tool authorization design;
  • an end-to-end evidence trace;
  • an outcome-event loop feeding Customer Intelligence.

The resulting separation is deliberate:

  • Banking systems remain authoritative for customers, accounts, payments, cases, complaints, and regulated decisions.
  • Customer Intelligence provides purpose-bound context, service events, derived understanding, and outcome history.
  • The AI platform provides governed model access, knowledge retrieval, evaluation, AI safety controls, registries, and observability.
  • The AI workflow and tool-use layer provides controlled workflow state, tool use, delegated authority, checkpoints, and execution evidence.
  • The journey application owns the employee experience, business logic, and customer-service outcome.

This end-to-end pilot gives IT a concrete solution to estimate and challenge while establishing reusable foundations for broader customer intelligence and future authenticated self-service.

IT architecture

Customer Intelligence–Enabled Service Resolution — Journey Technical Profiles

Purpose

The three candidate journeys use the common Technical Pilot Blueprint while retaining distinct banking systems, information boundaries, knowledge, tools, critical risks and validation requirements. Bank-specific products, APIs, data platforms and AI runtimes remain discovery decisions.

Each profile states:

  • which banking capabilities and authoritative information are required;
  • how that information is used by deterministic services and GenAI;
  • which knowledge and tools are permitted;
  • which information and decisions remain outside the AI-assisted workflow;
  • how the journey degrades or narrows when a capability is unavailable;
  • what IT must demonstrate before controlled live use.

Actual system names, owners, interfaces, volumes, service expectations, and selected products are completed during bank capability discovery.

Shared architecture and journey-specific boundaries

The common platform stays stable. Each overlay replaces the journey system, state model, information boundary, knowledge corpus, permitted tools, critical errors, and outcome definition.

Profile completion rule

Before a profile becomes implementation-ready, IT and the Journey Process Owner record:

Required decision What must be established
Authoritative sources named system or governed service for every displayed state, deadline, document/evidence status and outcome
Identity and linkage identifiers and matching rules connecting customer, journey object, case and contacts; quarantine behavior for uncertainty
Integration path existing API/event, controlled façade, or governed extract; freshness, supported use and owner
Context contract allow-listed fields, provenance, classifications, exclusions, freshness and retention
State interpretation recognized process states, transitions, blockers, exceptions and permitted customer-facing language
Knowledge product approved sources, owners, effective dates, access, withdrawal and retrieval tests
Tool authority read and write tools, prerequisites, limits, confirmation, idempotency, evidence and prohibited actions
Evaluation profile representative states, material exceptions, critical-error definitions, locked cases and live sampling
Operating dependency expected availability, latency, volume, fallback, support owner and suspension path appropriate to the pilot

If an authoritative source, safe information boundary, or supported live interface cannot be established, the journey remains historical or silent-evaluation only or is narrowed to the states that can be supported. GenAI must not compensate for a missing source of truth.

Payment Issue Resolution profile

Business charter: Payment Issue Resolution

Technical intent and boundary

Support one domestic retail-payment type with failed, pending, or reversed states for which the bank can obtain an authoritative status and an established servicing response. Unrecognized payments, fraud, disputes/chargebacks, sanctions or AML holds, cross-border/correspondent ambiguity, reimbursement decisions, and funds movement remain outside the profile.

Required bank capabilities and use

Required capability How the profile uses it If the capability is unavailable or unreliable
Customer/contact source identify the customer request and related contacts restrict to historical linked cases or stop live use where linkage cannot be trusted
Payment source of truth obtain payment identifier, type, timestamps and authoritative failed/pending/reversed state exclude the unsupported state or payment type; do not infer state from contact notes
Case or investigation workflow obtain owner, completed/pending service step and resolution; create an approved referral or note operate read-only and retain the existing manual write process
Complaint/escalation record identify formal complaint or specialist handling already in progress route possible complaints to the existing complaint check before advice
Payment-service knowledge ground state explanations, expected process and permitted action restrict output to verified facts and manual procedure lookup until the corpus is approved
Outcome reporting identify repeat contact, progression, reopen, complaint and handling effort run technical and quality validation only; do not claim customer benefit until outcome evidence is available

Functional allocation

Function Realization
Deterministic customer/payment/case linkage, authoritative status, eligibility, state-code mapping, freshness, permitted-action filtering
GenAI contact-history interpretation, concise timeline, likely service blocker, procedure-supported explanation and draft next step
Knowledge retrieval (RAG) current payment-state guidance, servicing procedure, communication wording, referral and escalation rules
Permitted tools read payment/case/contact state; record feedback/outcome; draft note; create an employee-approved referral where an existing API supports it
Critical exclusions state change, funds movement, fraud/dispute decision, reimbursement, regulated hold interpretation, autonomous customer communication

Journey-specific technical validation

  • Payment, customer, contact and case records link correctly or are quarantined.
  • The displayed payment state always comes from the authoritative source and carries freshness.
  • Each supported state maps to a Journey Process Owner-approved explanation and action set.
  • Conflicting status, missing investigation ownership, fraud/dispute indicators and excluded payment types route to the correct manual or specialist path.
  • Historical, silent and live evaluation separately measure state accuracy, action accuracy, unsupported explanation, employee correction and repeat-contact outcome.

Card Dispute Progress Support profile

Business charter: Card Dispute Progress Support

Technical intent and boundary

Support one dispute type and service queue by explaining authoritative dispute stage, completed actions, evidence state, responsible owner, applicable deadline, and permitted next service step. Adjudication, fraud determination, eligibility, reimbursement, legal interpretation, or alteration of scheme/statutory obligations remain outside the profile.

Required bank capabilities and use

Required capability How the profile uses it If the capability is unavailable or unreliable
Dispute system of record obtain dispute identifier, type, stage, milestones, owner and authoritative deadline data exclude states lacking authoritative stage/deadline information; retain specialist handling
Transaction reference connect the dispute to the correct card transaction without deciding fraud quarantine ambiguous linkage and route to existing verification
Evidence metadata show evidence type, request, receipt and validation status without unnecessary document content limit the profile to stage/status explanation; do not generate evidence requests from incomplete metadata
Communication record identify notices already sent and required servicing communications require manual confirmation against the dispute system before communication
Effective dispute knowledge retrieve the applicable internal and scheme-approved servicing procedure remain in silent evaluation for next-step generation until authority and effective dates are controlled
Outcome and deadline monitoring measure status contacts, evidence rework, handoff, complaint and missed-deadline events restrict the decision to quality/workflow learning; no scale decision on customer benefit

Function Realization
Deterministic dispute/customer/transaction linkage, authoritative stage, deadline calculation or source value, evidence status, required-notice and permitted-action rules
GenAI prior-contact summarization, status explanation, identification of repeated/conflicting evidence requests, procedure-grounded next-step draft
Knowledge retrieval (RAG) effective dispute-servicing procedure, evidence guidance, required communication and escalation conditions
Permitted tools read dispute/evidence/communication state; record feedback and outcome; draft evidence request; create employee-approved specialist referral where supported

Journey-specific technical validation

  • Dispute, transaction, customer and contact linkage is correct or quarantined.
  • Stage, evidence status, owner and deadline are authoritative, current and replayable.
  • No generated interpretation changes a deadline, customer right, adjudication state or reimbursement decision.
  • Any deadline, scheme-rule or evidence ambiguity triggers specialist fallback before customer communication.
  • Evaluation explicitly covers every common stage, evidence state, deadline boundary, prior-notice condition and material exception available for the selected dispute type.

Onboarding/KYC Progress Support profile

Business charter: Onboarding/KYC Progress Support

Technical intent and boundary

Support one customer segment and onboarding path using an approved customer-servicing metadata projection. Explain only established service state, permitted outstanding information, responsible queue and approved next step. The service resolution solution must not receive or infer restricted financial-crime rationale.

Journey-specific technical validation

  • Architecture tests demonstrate that excluded restricted fields and content have no path into context, retrieval, prompts, traces or employee output.
  • The displayed service state, permitted reason code, document status and queue come from the approved projection and carry source/freshness evidence.
  • The capability cannot infer, expose or imply a regulated reason for delay, approval or rejection.
  • Inconsistent state, missing permitted reason, vulnerability, potential discriminatory treatment or financial-crime concern routes to a specialist.
  • Evaluation covers common onboarding states, repeated requests, reason-code gaps, restricted-data injection attempts and relevant cohort outcomes.

This division is the practical platform test. A second journey should reuse the common interfaces while replacing its overlay. Where reuse requires copying or bypassing the common services, the platform contract has not yet been proven.

IT architecture

Customer Intelligence–Enabled Service Resolution — Platform Capability and Readiness Map

Purpose

Define the shared IT capabilities required to implement the Technical Pilot Blueprint and its journey technical profiles, without assuming the bank's current products, maturity, deployment model, or interface availability.

Vendor and low-level runtime selection follows bank capability discovery. The project first determines whether each required capability can be reused, extended, supplied as a controlled pilot component, or cannot safely support the proposed scope.

How the bank assesses each capability

Every capability receives one recorded disposition:

  • Reuse: an existing supported bank service satisfies the pilot need.
  • Extend: an existing service can satisfy it through a limited enhancement.
  • Pilot-local: a temporary implementation is permitted behind the intended enterprise contract.
  • Narrow/block: the journey or live mode is reduced because a safe dependency cannot be supplied.

Decisions required before solution commitment

The bank does not need every target platform capability before the pilot. It must make the following decisions explicitly:

Decision Required record

Product and framework choices are documented as architecture decisions after discovery. They must satisfy the contracts in the common blueprint and remain replaceable where the market or bank strategy is unsettled.

Minimum technical readiness gates

Architecture readiness

  • Selected journey profile is completed and consistent with its business charter.
  • Capability dispositions, enterprise interfaces, temporary components and owners are recorded.
  • Journey-specific logic is separated from shared platform capabilities.

Data and integration readiness

  • Authoritative sources, identifiers, status semantics and supported integration paths are confirmed.
  • Context and knowledge allow-lists, exclusions, freshness and quality behavior are tested.
  • Historical evaluation data and outcome measurement can be produced for the selected scope.

Control readiness

  • Identity, purpose, field access, model route, retrieval, output and tool decisions are enforced and evidenced.
  • Journey-specific prohibited data, decisions and actions are technically blocked.
  • Threat, privacy, conduct, incident, suspension and material-change decisions are recorded.

Operational readiness

  • Environments, deployment, secrets, telemetry, dependency monitoring, fallback and support are exercised.
  • The existing manual service remains available when AI, knowledge or source dependencies fail.
  • Workload and model observations are sufficient for controlled-live capacity, without implying premature scale hardware.

Quality readiness

  • Common states and material exceptions pass the approved historical and silent evaluation.
  • Critical errors defined by the selected profile do not pass the release gate.
  • Employee workflow, correction, escalation and outcome capture operate end to end.

CTO decision on reusable platform capabilities

Promotion requires evidence of a real second consumer, stable interface, named product owner, independent service expectation, support, cost and lifecycle. The CTO receives:

  • current bank capabilities successfully reused;
  • gaps filled temporarily by the pilot;
  • components that remain journey-specific;
  • shared capabilities ready for productization;
  • quality, security, resilience, cost and portability evidence;
  • target owners and an ordered investment recommendation.

This makes the pilot a deliberate first platform consumer and evidence generator. It does not assume that every temporary component deserves to become part of the long-term platform.
